requirements.title: Fork tests against real deployed dependencies

evidence.description: Swapr Algebra NFPM smoke test proves exact add-time caller balance deltas, zero adapter residue, zero residual position-manager allowances, real zero-liquidity fee materialization preserving position liquidity and NFT identity, and fee drainage before principal removal; it also proves the public-vault manager preserves its spot NFT across a partial exit and clears it on the final exit, and covers full-unwind spot and source-activated fresh-pool conditional public-vault gas checks.

Real direct-Algebra removal proves zero-liquidity fee realization preserves liquidity and drains fees before an immediate principal removal, fee-bearing partial removal at 116,245 gas under a 150,000-gas bound, final removal, pair isolation, donation accounting, and the mutable-cooldown liveness failure.

Real Uniswap V3 integration exercises adapter-owned fresh pool creation, initialization, and first-NFT mint; proves zero-liquidity live-fee materialization preserves liquidity and NFT identity and drains fees before an immediate principal removal; and rejects reuse of the initialized pool.

A pinned Ethereum-mainnet fork verifies the official v4 PoolManager runtime code hash and proves the exact initialization-gate ABI rejects outsider preinitialization before accepting the bound adapter on the same pool key.

A pinned Ethereum-mainnet fork proves the direct v4 adapter initializes and adds through the official PoolManager, realizes a third-party donation as fees, and performs sequential proportional and final removal without residue.
Real futarchy proposal, Reality question, and CTF condition wiring fork test.
Futarchy conditional router split behavior fork test.
Shared Algebra stability guard resolves and checks the live GNO/sDAI spot pool over its 30-minute window.
Fork tests are documented as a required final target-address check.

remaining: Run the fork test suite against the selected final target proposal and token addresses before limited-funds execution.

requirements.title: Invariant and fuzz coverage for accounting and safety properties

evidence.description: Core manager tests cover constructor rejection of an identical company/collateral token and code-less dependencies, independent rejection of every outcome-to-outcome and outcome-to-base alias before spot movement, every independent base/YES/NO token-ordering parity, proportional principal/fee/idle accounting with adversarial receipt-label misclassification, exact two-phase adapter-removal deltas with spot and conditional overreport rollback, divergent YES/NO liquidity and post-swap principal composition, sequential six-token conservation and nondecreasing survivor value per share, rejection of a nonfinal all-zero liquidity plan without burning the dust holder's shares followed by successful redemption after aggregation, complete rollback and identical-retry success when the final recipient payout fails after removal, share burn, and complete-set merging, exact settlement after randomized one-to-four partial exits, donation-resistant deposit pricing, spot and conditional six-token post-exit fee/donation ownership, resolved-wrapper donation recovery before spot redemption, deposit pricing, and later activation, rejection of direct native transfers outside that accounting model while wrapper unwrapping remains live, second-pool activation rollback, per-underlying conditional merge isolation with approval-failure, partial-consumption, and underpayment fallback, exact-delta merge and winner underconsumption/underpayment, late second-underlying rollback of prior recovery, losing-wrapper settlement rollback including after zero-supply final redemption, owner-authorized delayed permissionless non-custodial emergency exit, and permissionless settlement while emergency mode is armed or executed.
Factory tests prove constructor rejection of code-less shared dependencies and that identical or code-less company-token manager wiring rolls back the permissionless bundle.

The v4 factory suite proves caller-bound CREATE2 prediction and hook permissions, exact source/hook/adapter/manager bindings, front-run salt separation, mutation rejection, and complete rollback when the final manager deployment fails.

A pinned Ethereum-mainnet fork drives the factory-deployed source, official v3 position manager, canonical Conditional Tokens, deployed Wrapped1155 factory, router, manager, and two conditional positions through atomic activation and settlement against the official v4 PoolManager. Ten fault variants independently revert spot principal removal, each CTF split, wrapper conversion on each underlying, each v4 initialization and first-liquidity call, and source capture verification after activation completes; they compare actual protocol custody and position state as well as manager accounting, then prove the identical proposal activates after every fault is cleared. A late redemption-removal fault occurs after the first proportional official-v4 unwind and proves shares, positions, spot identity, and all six holder/manager/PoolManager balances restore. Its identical retry makes the canonical company-side CTF merge revert, proves collateral still merges while the company slice is paid as exact YES/NO wrappers, then redeems the winner, consumes the loser, settles the survivor, and conserves both assets through final exit. A late settlement fault occurs after both v4 removals and canonical company merge/winner recovery, then proves manager binding/accounting, adapter positions, PoolManager balances, CTF collateral/underlying custody, wrapper supply/custody, and allowances all roll back before the identical settlement succeeds. A conditional emergency run faults the second adapter removal after the first official-v4 unwind, proves positions, custody, accounting, shares, and the emergency flag roll back, then lets the same unrelated caller retry with zero gain, a shareholder redeem proportionally while canonical CTF remains unresolved, and the survivor settle permissionlessly after the source registry is cleared. Two spot-mode emergency runs separately fault official-v3 principal removal after fee collection and NFT burn after fee collection, full principal removal, and principal collection. Both prove the NFT/liquidity, manager/adapter/v3-pool/NPM balances, shares, and emergency flag restore, then complete the identical outsider retry with zero gain and recover both bootstrap assets within two wei.
The production router test proves exact CTF split receipts and exact wrapper mint deltas.

The official proposal source test proves that every outcome-to-outcome and outcome-to-base alias is rejected, every captured activation field must match the validated snapshot, and a corrupt capture rolls back both source and target state.

Deadline proxy tests prove the post-deadline fallback relays an already-finalized Reality result, fails closed when a normal finalized result is unavailable, and forces NO for unresolved state including a normal answer still inside its challenge window, pending arbitration, and Reality's canonical unresolved-answer sentinel.

The real source-manager-router binding test proves already-resolved-condition, first-conditional-add, canonical fresh-pool identity, first- and second-CTF-split, second-fresh-position, and external post-activation resolver-binding rollback across coordinator state, registry, spot position, manager binding, CTF collateral, wrapper total supply and custody, base custody, router allowances, and fresh pools; and exact-replay or second-live-proposal rejection without changing active positions or binding.
Adapter over-pull safety test.

Deterministic Uniswap V3 adapter tests separate fee-only, partial-principal, and final-principal removal fields exactly; cover fresh create-initialize-first-mint ownership; reject uninitialized and initialized guarded/manipulated-price pre-existing pools before custody changes; and prove distinct pool-creation, initialization, and first-mint failures roll back pool creation, initialization, balances, and approvals.

The selector-frozen v4 initialization gate enables only the before-initialize hook bit, binds once to a code-bearing adapter, rejects direct and wrong-key callbacks, prevents outsider preinitialization, and still lets the bound adapter initialize the same predictable key.

The selector-frozen direct v4 adapter tests exact prefunded settlement, donation fees, sequential partial/final removal, atomic initialization rollback, PoolManager codehash drift, dishonest poke reports, second-phase fee leakage, and manager-only operation.
Algebra guard tests cover inclusive 50-tick boundaries, signed TWAP rounding, and fail-closed history reads.

The initialized invariant harness interleaves deposits, activation, fees, donations, redemptions, CTF settlement, and emergency arm, disarm, and permissionless execution; settlement remains available during emergency mode, every successful deposit and redemption checks survivor-favoring liquidity and six-token balance ratios, and global invariants enforce conditional binding, adapter-liquidity consistency, known custody of all six issued tokens, zero managed residue at zero share supply, and zero position liquidity after emergency execution.
Independent integer properties prove that deposit floor/ceiling rounding cannot dilute either base asset and that partial liquidity, idle, and fee floor rounding favors survivors.
Deeper invariant pass command is documented for pre-deploy review.

remaining: Run the deeper invariant pass documented in docs/readiness.md before mainnet-value deployment.
